en: I'm going to talk to you about optimism
zh: 我要和大家聊聊乐观主义。

en: or more precisely, the optimism bias.
zh: 或者更准确地说，是乐观偏见。

en: It's a cognitive illusion
zh: 这是一种认知错觉。

en: that we've been studying in my lab for the past few years,
zh: 过去几年，我们一直在实验室里研究它。

en: and 80 percent of us have it.
zh: 而我们当中有80%的人都有这种错觉。

en: It's our tendency to overestimate
zh: 它指的是我们倾向于高估

en: our likelihood of experiencing good events in our lives
zh: 自己人生中遇到好事的可能性，

en: and underestimate our likelihood of experiencing bad events.
zh: 同时低估自己遇到坏事的可能性。

en: So we underestimate our likelihood of suffering from cancer,
zh: 所以，我们会低估自己患癌的可能性，

en: being in a car accident.
zh: 也会低估自己遭遇车祸的可能性。

en: We overestimate our longevity, our career prospects.
zh: 我们会高估自己的寿命，也会高估自己的职业前景。

en: In short, we're more optimistic than realistic,
zh: 简而言之，我们往往比现实情况更乐观，

en: but we are oblivious to the fact.
zh: 但我们自己却没有意识到这一点。

en: Take marriage for example.
zh: 拿婚姻来说。

en: In the Western world, divorce rates are about 40 percent.
zh: 在西方世界，离婚率大约是40%。

en: That means that out of five married couples,
zh: 这意味着每五对已婚夫妻中，

en: two will end up splitting their assets.
zh: 就有两对最终会分割财产、各奔东西。

en: But when you ask newlyweds about their own likelihood of divorce,
zh: 但是当你问新婚夫妇自己离婚的可能性有多大时，

en: they estimate it at zero percent.
zh: 他们的估计是零。

en: And even divorce lawyers, who should really know better,
zh: 甚至连本该更清楚这一点的离婚律师，

en: hugely underestimate their own likelihood of divorce.
zh: 也会大大低估自己离婚的可能性。

en: So it turns out that optimists are not less likely to divorce,
zh: 所以事实证明，乐观主义者并不更不容易离婚，

en: but they are more likely to remarry.
zh: 但他们更有可能再婚。

en: In the words of Samuel Johnson,
zh: 用 Samuel Johnson 的话来说，

en: "Remarriage is the triumph of hope over experience."
zh: '再婚，是希望战胜经验的胜利。'

en: So if we're married, we're more likely to have kids.
zh: 所以，如果我们结了婚，我们更有可能会有孩子。

en: And we all think our kids will be especially talented.
zh: 而我们都觉得自己的孩子会特别有天赋。

en: This, by the way, is my two-year-old nephew, Guy.
zh: 顺便说一下，这是我两岁的侄子 Guy。

en: And I just want to make it absolutely clear
zh: 我只想非常明确地说明一点，

en: that he's a really bad example of the optimism bias,
zh: 他实在不是乐观偏见的好例子，

en: because he is in fact uniquely talented.
zh: 因为事实上，他确实有独一无二的天赋。

en: And I'm not alone.
zh: 而且不只是我这样想。

en: Out of four British people, three said
zh: 每四个英国人当中，就有三个人说

en: that they were optimistic about the future of their own families.
zh: 他们对自己家庭的未来感到乐观。

en: That's 75 percent.
zh: 也就是75%。

en: But only 30 percent said
zh: 但只有30%的人说，

en: that they thought families in general
zh: 他们认为总体来看，家庭的状况

en: are doing better than a few generations ago.
zh: 比几代人以前更好了。

en: And this is a really important point,
zh: 这是一个非常重要的点，

en: because we're optimistic about ourselves,
zh: 因为我们对自己很乐观，

en: we're optimistic about our kids,
zh: 对自己的孩子很乐观，

en: we're optimistic about our families,
zh: 对自己的家庭也很乐观，

en: but we're not so optimistic about the guy sitting next to us,
zh: 但我们对坐在旁边的那个人就没那么乐观了，

en: and we're somewhat pessimistic
zh: 而且我们对

en: about the fate of our fellow citizens and the fate of our country.
zh: 同胞的命运和国家的命运多少有些悲观。

en: But private optimism about our own personal future
zh: 但是，我们对自己个人未来的私人乐观，

en: remains persistent.
zh: 却始终存在。

en: And it doesn't mean that we think things will magically turn out okay,
zh: 这并不是说我们觉得事情会神奇地自己变好，

en: but rather that we have the unique ability to make it so.
zh: 而是说，我们相信自己有独特的能力让事情变好。

en: Now I'm a scientist, I do experiments.
zh: 我是科学家，我做实验。

en: So to show you what I mean,
zh: 所以为了让大家明白我的意思，

en: I'm going to do an experiment here with you.
zh: 我想在这里和大家做一个实验。

en: So I'm going to give you a list of abilities and characteristics,
zh: 我会给大家列出一组能力和特质，

en: and I want you to think for each of these abilities
zh: 我希望大家针对每一项能力想一想，

en: where you stand relative to the rest of the population.
zh: 自己和其他人相比处在什么位置。

en: The first one is getting along well with others.
zh: 第一项是与他人相处融洽的能力。

en: Who here believes they're at the bottom 25 percent?
zh: 在座有谁认为自己处在后25%？

en: Okay, that's about 10 people out of 1,500.
zh: 好，大约是1500人里的10个人。

en: Who believes they're at the top 25 percent?
zh: 有谁认为自己处在前25%？

en: That's most of us here.
zh: 这里大多数人都是这样认为的。

en: Okay, now do the same for your driving ability.
zh: 好，现在请用同样的方法评估一下你的驾驶能力。

en: How interesting are you?
zh: 你有多有趣？

en: How attractive are you?
zh: 你有多有吸引力？

en: How honest are you?
zh: 你有多诚实？

en: And finally, how modest are you?
zh: 最后，你有多谦虚？

en: So most of us put ourselves above average
zh: 所以在大多数这些能力上，我们大多数人

en: on most of these abilities.
zh: 都会把自己放在平均水平以上。

en: Now this is statistically impossible.
zh: 但从统计学上来说，这是不可能的。

en: We can't all be better than everyone else.
zh: 我们不可能全都比其他人更优秀。

en: But if we believe we're better than the other guy,
zh: 可是，如果我们相信自己比别人更优秀，

en: well that means that we're more likely to get that promotion, to remain married,
zh: 那就意味着我们更有可能获得升职，也更有可能维持婚姻，

en: because we're more social, more interesting.
zh: 因为我们更善于社交，也更有趣。

en: And it's a global phenomenon.
zh: 而这是一种全球现象。

en: The optimism bias has been observed
zh: 乐观偏见已经被观察到

en: in many different countries --
zh: 存在于许多不同的国家——

en: in Western cultures, in non-Western cultures,
zh: 存在于西方文化中，也存在于非西方文化中，

en: in females and males,
zh: 存在于女性和男性当中，

en: in kids, in the elderly.
zh: 存在于儿童和老年人当中。

en: It's quite widespread.
zh: 它相当普遍。

en: But the question is, is it good for us?
zh: 但问题是，它对我们有好处吗？

en: So some people say no.
zh: 有些人说没有。

en: Some people say the secret to happiness
zh: 有些人说，幸福的秘诀

en: is low expectations.
zh: 就是降低期待。

en: I think the logic goes something like this:
zh: 我想这个逻辑大概是这样的：

en: If we don't expect greatness,
zh: 如果我们不期待伟大的事情，

en: if we don't expect to find love and be healthy and successful,
zh: 如果我们不期待找到爱情、保持健康、获得成功，

en: well we're not going to be disappointed when these things don't happen.
zh: 那么当这些事情没有发生时，我们就不会失望。

en: And if we're not disappointed when good things don't happen,
zh: 如果好事没有发生时我们不会失望，

en: and we're pleasantly surprised when they do,
zh: 而当好事真的发生时，我们又会感到惊喜，

en: we will be happy.
zh: 那我们就会幸福。

en: So it's a very good theory,
zh: 所以这是一个很好的理论，

en: but it turns out to be wrong for three reasons.
zh: 但事实证明，它错了，原因有三个。

en: Number one: Whatever happens, whether you succeed or you fail,
zh: 第一：无论发生什么，无论你成功还是失败，

en: people with high expectations always feel better.
zh: 期待更高的人总是感觉更好。

en: Because how we feel when we get dumped or win employee of the month
zh: 因为当我们被甩，或者被评为月度员工时，心里是什么感受，

en: depends on how we interpret that event.
zh: 取决于我们如何解读这件事。

en: The psychologists Margaret Marshall and John Brown
zh: 心理学家 Margaret Marshall 和 John Brown

en: studied students with high and low expectations.
zh: 研究了高期待和低期待的学生。

en: And they found that when people with high expectations succeed,
zh: 他们发现，当高期待的人取得成功时，

en: they attribute that success to their own traits.
zh: 他们会把成功归因于自己的特质。

en: "I'm a genius, therefore I got an A,
zh: '我是个天才，所以我拿了A，

en: therefore I'll get an A again and again in the future."
zh: 所以以后我还会一次又一次拿A。'

en: When they failed, it wasn't because they were dumb,
zh: 当他们失败时，那并不是因为他们笨，

en: but because the exam just happened to be unfair.
zh: 而是因为考试刚好不公平。

en: Next time they will do better.
zh: 下次他们会做得更好。

en: People with low expectations do the opposite.
zh: 低期待的人则正好相反。

en: So when they failed it was because they were dumb,
zh: 所以当他们失败时，是因为他们笨，

en: and when they succeeded
zh: 而当他们成功时，

en: it was because the exam just happened to be really easy.
zh: 那是因为考试刚好真的很简单。

en: Next time reality would catch up with them.
zh: 下次现实就会让他们露馅。

en: So they felt worse.
zh: 所以他们感觉更糟。

en: Number two: Regardless of the outcome,
zh: 第二：无论结果如何，

en: the pure act of anticipation makes us happy.
zh: 单纯的期待本身就会让我们快乐。

en: The behavioral economist George Lowenstein
zh: 行为经济学家 George Lowenstein

en: asked students in his university
zh: 让他所在大学的学生

en: to imagine getting a passionate kiss from a celebrity, any celebrity.
zh: 想象自己得到一位名人的热吻，任何名人都可以。

en: Then he said, "How much are you willing to pay
zh: 然后他说：如果要得到一位名人的吻，

en: to get a kiss from a celebrity
zh: 你愿意付多少钱？

en: if the kiss was delivered immediately,
zh: 如果这个吻是立刻给你，

en: in three hours, in 24 hours, in three days,
zh: 或者三小时后、二十四小时后、三天后，

en: in one year, in 10 years?
zh: 一年后、十年后呢？'

en: He found that the students were willing to pay the most
zh: 他发现，学生愿意付最多钱的，

en: not to get a kiss immediately,
zh: 并不是立刻得到这个吻，

en: but to get a kiss in three days.
zh: 而是三天后得到这个吻。

en: They were willing to pay extra in order to wait.
zh: 他们愿意多付钱，来换取等待。

en: Now they weren't willing to wait a year or 10 years;
zh: 当然，他们并不愿意等一年或十年；

en: no one wants an aging celebrity.
zh: 没人想要一个已经变老的名人。

en: But three days seemed to be the optimum amount.
zh: 但三天似乎是最理想的时长。

en: So why is that?
zh: 这是为什么呢？

en: Well if you get the kiss now, it's over and done with.
zh: 如果你现在就得到这个吻，那它就结束了。

en: But if you get the kiss in three days,
zh: 但如果你三天后才得到这个吻，

en: well that's three days of jittery anticipation, the thrill of the wait.
zh: 那你就会有三天紧张又兴奋的期待，有等待带来的刺激感。

en: The students wanted that time
zh: 学生们想要这段时间，

en: to imagine where is it going to happen,
zh: 去想象这件事会在哪里发生，

en: how is it going to happen.
zh: 又会怎样发生。

en: Anticipation made them happy.
zh: 期待让他们感到快乐。

en: This is, by the way, why people prefer Friday to Sunday.
zh: 顺便说一下，这也是为什么人们更喜欢周五，而不是周日。

en: It's a really curious fact,
zh: 这是一个非常有意思的事实，

en: because Friday is a day of work and Sunday is a day of pleasure,
zh: 因为周五是工作日，而周日是享乐的日子，

en: so you'd assume that people will prefer Sunday,
zh: 所以你可能会以为人们更喜欢周日，

en: but they don't.
zh: 但他们并不是。

en: It's not because they really, really like being in the office
zh: 这并不是因为他们真的非常非常喜欢待在办公室，

en: and they can't stand strolling in the park
zh: 也不是因为他们受不了在公园散步，

en: or having a lazy brunch.
zh: 或者受不了悠闲地吃一顿早午餐。

en: We know that, because when you ask people
zh: 我们知道这一点，是因为当你问人们

en: about their ultimate favorite day of the week,
zh: 他们一周中最喜欢哪一天时，

en: surprise, surprise, Saturday comes in at first,
zh: 毫不意外，周六排第一，

en: then Friday, then Sunday.
zh: 然后是周五，再然后是周日。

en: People prefer Friday
zh: 人们更喜欢周五，

en: because Friday brings with it the anticipation of the weekend ahead,
zh: 因为周五带来了对即将到来的周末的期待，

en: all the plans that you have.
zh: 以及你已经安排好的所有计划。

en: On Sunday, the only thing you can look forward to
zh: 而到了周日，你唯一可以期待的

en: is the work week.
zh: 就是接下来的一周工作。

en: So optimists are people who expect more kisses in their future,
zh: 所以，乐观主义者就是那些期待未来会有更多亲吻的人，

en: more strolls in the park.
zh: 期待未来会有更多公园散步的人。

en: And that anticipation enhances their wellbeing.
zh: 而这种期待会提升他们的幸福感。

en: In fact, without the optimism bias,
zh: 事实上，如果没有乐观偏见，

en: we would all be slightly depressed.
zh: 我们所有人都会有点抑郁。

en: People with mild depression,
zh: 轻度抑郁的人，

en: they don't have a bias when they look into the future.
zh: 在展望未来时并没有这种偏见。

en: They're actually more realistic than healthy individuals.
zh: 他们其实比健康个体更加现实。

en: But individuals with severe depression,
zh: 但重度抑郁的人，

en: they have a pessimistic bias.
zh: 则会有一种悲观偏见。

en: So they tend to expect the future
zh: 所以他们倾向于认为未来

en: to be worse than it ends up being.
zh: 会比实际结果更糟。

en: So optimism changes subjective reality.
zh: 因此，乐观会改变主观现实。

en: The way we expect the world to be changes the way we see it.
zh: 我们期待世界是什么样子，会改变我们看待世界的方式。

en: But it also changes objective reality.
zh: 但它也会改变客观现实。

en: It acts as a self-fulfilling prophecy.
zh: 它会成为一种自我实现的预言。

en: And that is the third reason
zh: 这就是第三个原因，

en: why lowering your expectations will not make you happy.
zh: 说明降低期待并不会让你幸福。

en: Controlled experiments have shown
zh: 受控实验已经表明，

en: that optimism is not only related to success,
zh: 乐观不仅与成功相关，

en: it leads to success.
zh: 它还会带来成功。

en: Optimism leads to success in academia and sports and politics.
zh: 乐观会带来学业、体育和政治上的成功。

en: And maybe the most surprising benefit of optimism is health.
zh: 而乐观也许最令人惊讶的好处，是对健康的影响。

en: If we expect the future to be bright,
zh: 如果我们期待未来是光明的，

en: stress and anxiety are reduced.
zh: 压力和焦虑就会减少。

en: So all in all, optimism has lots of benefits.
zh: 所以总的来说，乐观有很多好处。

en: But the question that was really confusing to me was,
zh: 但真正让我困惑的问题是，

en: how do we maintain optimism in the face of reality?
zh: 面对现实，我们是如何保持乐观的？

en: As an neuroscientist, this was especially confusing,
zh: 作为一名神经科学家，这一点尤其让我困惑，

en: because according to all the theories out there,
zh: 因为根据现有的所有理论，

en: when your expectations are not met, you should alter them.
zh: 当你的期待没有实现时，你应该调整期待。

en: But this is not what we find.
zh: 但我们发现的并不是这样。

en: We asked people to come into our lab
zh: 我们请人来到实验室，

en: in order to try and figure out what was going on.
zh: 试图弄清楚到底发生了什么。

en: We asked them to estimate their likelihood
zh: 我们让他们估计自己

en: of experiencing different terrible events in their lives.
zh: 在一生中经历各种可怕事件的可能性。

en: So, for example, what is your likelihood of suffering from cancer?
zh: 比如说，你患癌的可能性有多大？

en: And then we told them the average likelihood
zh: 然后我们告诉他们，像他们这样的人

en: of someone like them to suffer these misfortunes.
zh: 遭遇这些不幸的平均概率是多少。

en: So cancer, for example, is about 30 percent.
zh: 比如癌症，大约是30%。

en: And then we asked them again,
zh: 然后我们再次问他们：

en: "How likely are you to suffer from cancer?"
zh: '你患癌的可能性有多大？'

en: What we wanted to know was
zh: 我们想知道的是，

en: whether people will take the information that we gave them
zh: 人们是否会利用我们给他们的信息，

en: to change their beliefs.
zh: 来改变自己的信念。

en: And indeed they did --
zh: 而事实上，他们确实会——

en: but mostly when the information we gave them
zh: 但主要是在我们给他们的信息

en: was better than what they expected.
zh: 比他们预期的要好。

en: So for example,
zh: 比如说，

en: if someone said, "My likelihood of suffering from cancer
zh: 如果有人说：我患癌症的可能性

en: is about 50 percent,"
zh: 大约是50%。

en: and we said, "Hey, good news.
zh: 然后我们说：嘿，好消息。

en: The average likelihood is only 30 percent,"
zh: 平均概率只有30%。'

en: the next time around they would say,
zh: 下一轮他们就会说：

en: "Well maybe my likelihood is about 35 percent."
zh: '嗯，也许我的概率大概是35%。'

en: So they learned quickly and efficiently.
zh: 所以他们学得又快又有效。

en: But if someone started off saying,
zh: 但如果有人一开始说：

en: "My average likelihood of suffering from cancer is about 10 percent,"
zh: '我患癌症的平均可能性大约是10%。'

en: and we said, "Hey, bad news.
zh: 然后我们说：嘿，坏消息。

en: The average likelihood is about 30 percent,"
zh: 平均概率大约是30%。'

en: the next time around they would say,
zh: 下一轮他们会说：

en: "Yep. Still think it's about 11 percent."
zh: '嗯。还是觉得大概是11%。'

en: So it's not that they didn't learn at all -- they did --
zh: 所以并不是说他们完全没学到——他们确实学到了——

en: but much, much less than when we gave them
zh: 只是比起我们给他们

en: positive information about the future.
zh: 关于未来的正面信息时，学到的要少得多。

en: And it's not that they didn't remember the numbers that we gave them;
zh: 而且也不是说他们不记得我们给出的数字；

en: everyone remembers that the average likelihood of cancer
zh: 每个人都记得患癌症的平均概率

en: is about 30 percent
zh: 大约是30%，

en: and the average likelihood of divorce is about 40 percent.
zh: 离婚的平均概率大约是40%。

en: But they didn't think that those numbers were related to them.
zh: 但他们并不认为这些数字和自己有关。

en: What this means is that warning signs such as these
zh: 这意味着，像这样的警示标志

en: may only have limited impact.
zh: 可能只能产生有限的影响。

en: Yes, smoking kills, but mostly it kills the other guy.
zh: 没错，吸烟会致命，但死的多半是别人。

en: What I wanted to know was
zh: 我想知道的是，

en: what was going on inside the human brain
zh: 人类大脑内部到底发生了什么，

en: that prevented us from taking these warning signs personally.
zh: 让我们无法把这些警示当成和自己有关的事。

en: But at the same time,
zh: 但与此同时，

en: when we hear that the housing market is hopeful,
zh: 当我们听说楼市前景乐观时，

en: we think, "Oh, my house is definitely going to double in price."
zh: 我们会想：哦，我的房子价格肯定会翻倍。

en: To try and figure that out,
zh: 为了弄清楚这一点，

en: I asked the participants in the experiment
zh: 我让实验参与者

en: to lie in a brain imaging scanner.
zh: 躺进脑成像扫描仪里。

en: It looks like this.
zh: 它看起来是这样的。

en: And using a method called functional MRI,
zh: 通过一种叫作功能性磁共振成像的方法，

en: we were able to identify regions in the brain
zh: 我们能够识别出大脑中

en: that were responding to positive information.
zh: 会对正面信息作出反应的区域。

en: One of these regions is called the left inferior frontal gyrus.
zh: 其中一个区域叫作左侧额下回。

en: So if someone said, "My likelihood of suffering from cancer is 50 percent,"
zh: 所以如果有人说：我患癌症的可能性是50%。

en: and we said, "Hey, good news.
zh: 然后我们说：嘿，好消息。

en: Average likelihood is 30 percent,"
zh: 平均概率是30%。

en: the left inferior frontal gyrus would respond fiercely.
zh: 左侧额下回就会作出强烈反应。

en: And it didn't matter if you're an extreme optimist, a mild optimist
zh: 而且不管你是极度乐观、轻度乐观，

en: or slightly pessimistic,
zh: 还是稍微有点悲观，

en: everyone's left inferior frontal gyrus
zh: 每个人的左侧额下回

en: was functioning perfectly well,
zh: 都运行得非常正常，

en: whether you're Barack Obama or Woody Allen.
zh: 无论你是Barack Obama还是Woody Allen。

en: On the other side of the brain,
zh: 而在大脑的另一侧，

en: the right inferior frontal gyrus was responding to bad news.
zh: 右侧额下回会对坏消息作出反应。

en: And here's the thing: it wasn't doing a very good job.
zh: 但问题是：它做得并不太好。

en: The more optimistic you were,
zh: 你越乐观，

en: the less likely this region was
zh: 这个区域就越不可能

en: to respond to unexpected negative information.
zh: 对意外的负面信息作出反应。

en: And if your brain is failing
zh: 如果你的大脑无法

en: at integrating bad news about the future,
zh: 整合关于未来的坏消息，

en: you will constantly leave your rose-tinted spectacles on.
zh: 你就会一直戴着玫瑰色眼镜看世界。

en: So we wanted to know, could we change this?
zh: 所以我们想知道，我们能改变这一点吗？

en: Could we alter people's optimism bias
zh: 我们能不能通过干扰这些区域的大脑活动，

en: by interfering with the brain activity in these regions?
zh: 来改变人们的乐观偏差？

en: And there's a way for us to do that.
zh: 而我们确实有办法做到。

en: This is my collaborator Ryota Kanai.
zh: 这是我的合作者Ryota Kanai。

en: And what he's doing is he's passing a small magnetic pulse
zh: 他正在做的是，让一个小小的磁脉冲

en: through the skull of the participant in our study
zh: 穿过我们研究参与者的颅骨，

en: into their inferior frontal gyrus.
zh: 进入他们的额下回。

en: And by doing that,
zh: 通过这样做，

en: he's interfering with the activity of this brain region
zh: 他会干扰这个脑区的活动，

en: for about half an hour.
zh: 持续大约半个小时。

en: After that everything goes back to normal, I assure you.
zh: 之后一切都会恢复正常，我向你们保证。

en: So let's see what happens.
zh: 那我们来看看会发生什么。

en: First of all, I'm going to show you
zh: 首先，我要给你们展示

en: the average amount of bias that we see.
zh: 我们观察到的平均偏差程度。

en: So if I was to test all of you now,
zh: 也就是说，如果我现在测试你们所有人，

en: this is the amount that you would learn
zh: 这就是你们会从好消息中学到的内容，

en: more from good news relative to bad news.
zh: 相比坏消息而言，多出来的程度。

en: Now we interfere with the region
zh: 接着，我们干扰了那个

en: that we found to integrate negative information in this task,
zh: 在这个任务中负责整合负面信息的区域，

en: and the optimism bias grew even larger.
zh: 结果乐观偏差变得更大了。

en: We made people more biased in the way that they process information.
zh: 我们让人们在处理信息的方式上变得更有偏差。

en: Then we interfered with the brain region
zh: 然后我们干扰了那个

en: that we found to integrate good news in this task,
zh: 在这个任务中负责整合好消息的脑区，

en: and the optimism bias disappeared.
zh: 结果乐观偏差消失了。

en: We were quite amazed by these results
zh: 这些结果让我们相当惊讶，

en: because we were able to eliminate
zh: 因为我们竟然能够消除

en: a deep-rooted bias in humans.
zh: 人类身上一种根深蒂固的偏差。

en: And at this point we stopped and we asked ourselves,
zh: 到这个时候，我们停下来问自己，

en: would we want to shatter the optimism illusion into tiny little bits?
zh: 我们真的想把乐观幻觉击得粉碎吗？

en: If we could do that, would we want to take people's optimism bias away?
zh: 如果我们能做到，我们真的想拿走人们的乐观偏差吗？

en: Well I've already told you about all of the benefits of the optimism bias,
zh: 我已经告诉过你们乐观偏差的种种好处，

en: which probably makes you want to hold onto it for dear life.
zh: 这大概会让你们想拼命留住它。

en: But there are, of course, pitfalls,
zh: 但当然，它也有陷阱，

en: and it would be really foolish of us to ignore them.
zh: 忽视这些陷阱会非常愚蠢。

en: Take for example this email I recieved
zh: 比如看看我收到的这封邮件，

en: from a firefighter here in California.
zh: 它来自加州这里的一名消防员。

en: He says, "Fatality investigations for firefighters
zh: 他说：消防员死亡事故调查中，

en: often include 'We didn't think the fire was going to do that,'
zh: 经常会出现‘我们没想到火势会那样发展’这句话，

en: even when all of the available information
zh: 尽管当时所有可用的信息

en: was there to make safe decisions."
zh: 都足以让他们作出安全的决定。'

en: This captain is going to use our findings on the optimism bias
zh: 这位队长打算利用我们关于乐观偏差的研究发现，

en: to try to explain to the firefighters
zh: 去向消防员解释

en: why they think the way they do,
zh: 为什么他们会那样思考，

en: to make them acutely aware of this very optimistic bias in humans.
zh: 让他们强烈意识到人类身上这种非常乐观的偏差。

en: So unrealistic optimism can lead to risky behavior,
zh: 所以，不现实的乐观可能导致冒险行为，

en: to financial collapse, to faulty planning.
zh: 导致金融崩溃，导致错误的规划。

en: The British government, for example,
zh: 比如英国政府

en: has acknowledged that the optimism bias
zh: 已经承认，乐观偏差

en: can make individuals more likely
zh: 会让个人更容易

en: to underestimate the costs and durations of projects.
zh: 低估项目的成本和工期。

en: So they have adjusted the 2012 Olympic budget
zh: 所以他们在制定2012年奥运会预算时，

en: for the optimism bias.
zh: 对乐观偏差作了调整。

en: My friend who's getting married in a few weeks
zh: 我有个朋友几周后要结婚，

en: has done the same for his wedding budget.
zh: 他也对自己的婚礼预算做了同样的处理。

en: And by the way, when I asked him about his own likelihood of divorce,
zh: 顺便说一句，当我问他自己离婚的可能性有多大时，

en: he said he was quite sure it was zero percent.
zh: 他说他非常确定是0%。

en: So what we would really like to do,
zh: 所以我们真正想做的是，

en: is we would like to protect ourselves from the dangers of optimism,
zh: 保护自己免受乐观的危险影响，

en: but at the same time remain hopeful,
zh: 但与此同时保持希望，

en: benefiting from the many fruits of optimism.
zh: 享受乐观带来的许多成果。

en: And I believe there's a way for us to do that.
zh: 我相信我们有办法做到这一点。

en: The key here really is knowledge.
zh: 这里真正的关键是知识。

en: We're not born with an innate understanding of our biases.
zh: 我们并不是天生就懂得自己的偏差。

en: These have to be identified by scientific investigation.
zh: 这些偏差必须通过科学研究来识别。

en: But the good news is that becoming aware of the optimism bias
zh: 但好消息是，意识到乐观偏差的存在

en: does not shatter the illusion.
zh: 并不会打破这种幻觉。

en: It's like visual illusions,
zh: 这就像视觉错觉一样，

en: in which understanding them does not make them go away.
zh: 你理解了它们，也不会让它们消失。

en: And this is good because it means
zh: 这是一件好事，因为它意味着

en: we should be able to strike a balance,
zh: 我们应该能够取得一种平衡，

en: to come up with plans and rules
zh: 制定计划和规则，

en: to protect ourselves from unrealistic optimism,
zh: 保护自己免受不现实乐观的影响，

en: but at the same time remain hopeful.
zh: 但同时仍然保持希望。

en: I think this cartoon portrays it nicely.
zh: 我觉得这幅漫画很好地表达了这一点。

en: Because if you're one of these pessimistic penguins up there
zh: 因为如果你是上面那些悲观的企鹅之一，

en: who just does not believe they can fly,
zh: 完全不相信自己能飞，

en: you certainly never will.
zh: 那你当然永远也飞不起来。

en: Because to make any kind of progress,
zh: 因为要取得任何进步，

en: we need to be able to imagine a different reality,
zh: 我们都需要能够想象一种不同的现实，

en: and then we need to believe that that reality is possible.
zh: 然后我们需要相信那种现实是可能的。

en: But if you are an extreme optimistic penguin
zh: 但如果你是一只极度乐观的企鹅，

en: who just jumps down blindly hoping for the best,
zh: 只是盲目跳下去，希望一切顺利，

en: you might find yourself in a bit of a mess when you hit the ground.
zh: 那你落地的时候，可能会发现自己有点麻烦。

en: But if you're an optimistic penguin
zh: 但如果你是一只乐观的企鹅，

en: who believes they can fly,
zh: 相信自己能飞，

en: but then adjusts a parachute to your back
zh: 但随后又在背上装好降落伞，

en: just in case things don't work out exactly as you had planned,
zh: 以防事情没有完全按你的计划发展，

en: you will soar like an eagle,
zh: 你就会像鹰一样翱翔，

en: even if you're just a penguin.
zh: 即便你只是一只企鹅。

en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢大家。
